page: Microsoft Azure D16lds_v5 is a compute-focused general-purpose virtual machine designed for workloads requiring a lower memory-to-vCPU allocation with fast scratch storage. Operating on Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance is powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at a base clock of 2.8 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 16 dedicated virtual CPUs derived from 8 physical cores via hyperthreading, backed by 48 MB of L3 cache and hardware support for AVX-512 with VNNI. The system is equipped with 32 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2 GB per core, along with 644 GB of direct-attached local SSD storage.

Benchmark evaluations position the D16lds_v5 within average ranges across standard CPU and system operations, returning a Geekbench multi-core score of 9941 and a PassMark CPU score of 21155.48. In vectorized execution, PassMark extended instructions reached 14154.52, supported by hardware AVX-512 extensions. Memory bandwidth achieves 102.63 GB/sec on uncached read blocks and 59.33 GB/sec on writes. For real-world services, it delivers 16.06 million Redis SET operations per second and 22.3 GB/sec in static web serving. Additionally, small language model text generation achieves a strong 274.55 tokens per second on a 135M parameter model.

The 1:2 memory configuration offers a cost-effective design for workloads that do not saturate standard 1:4 memory footprints, avoiding overprovisioned RAM expenses. However, the 32 GB memory limit poses constraints for large in-memory datasets or deep multi-tenant virtualization. The inclusion of 644 GB local SSD storage benefits applications demanding high-speed temporary caching, CI/CD compilation, batch data transformation, and distributed web serving tiers.
description: Microsoft Azure D16lds_v5 is an x86_64 virtual machine featuring an Intel Xeon 8370C processor with 16 dedicated vCPUs, 32 GB of RAM, and 644 GB of local SSD storage without bundled GPUs. Configured with a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this low-memory profile targets tasks that prioritize multi-threaded computation over large in-memory arrays. Benchmark tests demonstrate steady average performance across standard compute metrics, such as a PassMark CPU score of 21155.48 and 16.06 million Redis SET operations per second, along with strong small-model LLM generation throughput. The bundled fast local storage assists applications requiring quick disk access. The D16lds_v5 is well suited for code compilation pipelines, batch processing, static web serving, and distributed cache nodes that do not demand extensive RAM.
